content.method: Fit PCA on ID features, retain the low-variance eigenvectors `V_low`, and compute `r = np.linalg.norm((f - mu) @ V_low, axis=1)`; set `alpha = mean(max(id_logits, axis=1)) / mean(r_id)` and virtual logit `v = alpha*r`. Cosine support from the classifier-selected normalized prototype should be high for in-scope examples, but its typical level varies by predicted intent. Predicted-class conditional lower-tail calibration highlights angular mismatch without globally ranking examples solely by their nearest prototype similarity.

High predictive entropy and a large predicted-intent conditional local neighbor radius capture complementary uncertainty and feature-support failures. Train-fitted class-conditional empirical tail maps place both cues on a common scale without using evaluation statistics.

content.method: Predict \(\hat y=\arg\max_k \text{logits}_k\), compute the feature distance \(d=\lVert z-c_{\hat y}\rVert_2\) to that known class’s training-feature centroid \(c_{\hat y}\), and use \(s=d-r_{\hat y}\), where \(r_k\) is the learned class-specific adaptive boundary.  Classify as out-of-scope when \(s>0\) (otherwise retain \(\hat y\)); centroids and radii are estimated/learned from known-class training data.

content.rationale: Classifier-selected class density is calibrated separately for bottleneck and encoder views, so an input is anomalous when its predicted intent lacks support in either near-intent or broad-domain geometry.

A principal encoder subspace captures common in-scope variation, while the largest coordinate-level deviation left in its residual can expose sparse unsupported feature shifts that a residual L2 norm dilutes.

Normalized pooled encoder representations provide semantic local support beyond the bottleneck classifier space. A weighted average across near and moderately distant neighbors is less sensitive to duplicate examples or a single accidental neighbor than one k-th-neighbor radius.

Low-variance within-class directions are constrained for supported intents, and an OOS shift can produce a coherent excursion across several such directions. Random signed sketches detect these coherent trailing-subspace shifts rather than reducing them to a Mahalanobis radius.

A supported prediction should agree with feature geometry: its predicted intent should be nearly as close as the best class prototype. Class-conditional tail calibration flags classifier-to-representation disagreement without relying on eval statistics.

The difference between energy at two temperatures is invariant to a common logit shift and measures how concentrated the winning logit is relative to its competitors. Diffuse or atypical competition patterns receive a high predicted-class-calibrated tail score.

A supported classifier prediction should have stronger cosine alignment to its selected intent prototype than to competing intent prototypes. Class-conditional lower-tail calibration of this angular prototype margin flags unfamiliar or ambiguous intent geometry.

Classifier uncertainty and predicted-intent feature support are complementary signals. Class-conditional training tail probabilities put energy and bottleneck Mahalanobis residuals on a common scale before fusion.

The normalized Dirichlet concentration vector describes how evidence is allocated among intents independently of total evidence. A predicted-intent-specific two-sided tail score for concentration (Simpson) detects unusually diffuse or unusually concentrated evidential competition.

Confident predictions retain the energy score exactly, while energy-uncertain items are ranked by classifier-selected prototype support in encoder space. This exposes queries whose logits are uncertain and whose representation is also atypical for the predicted intent.

Intent-specific diagonal variances identify feature coordinates that are normally tightly constrained for the classifier-selected intent. A soft aggregate of unusually large coordinate-wise standardized residuals detects distributed support violations without collapsing them into a single Gaussian density.
The span of class centroids captures directions used to discriminate known intents, while local support in its orthogonal complement detects novel residual semantic content.

Bottleneck and pooled encoder distances capture near-intent and broader domain shifts, but their support scales can vary substantially by classifier-selected intent. Predicted-intent robust calibration followed by train-fitted covariance-aware additive weighting prevents one redundant view from dominating the fused anomaly signal.
The norm outside a principal subspace fitted only on in-scope encoder features measures representation components unsupported by the known-intent manifold, as in ViM-style residual scoring.

The normalized softmax vector encodes the full pattern of competition among intents, not just the winning confidence. A multiscale average of nearest in-scope predictive shapes flags queries whose classifier response is locally unsupported.

Within-class trailing covariance directions are tightly constrained for supported intents. Classifier-selected local support in whitened trailing residual directions detects unfamiliar OOS deviations.

A prediction is unreliable when its bottleneck representation lies beyond the class-specific support radius of the intent selected by the classifier. Class-adaptive centroids and radii account for intents with naturally different spread.

In-scope predictions tend to have characteristic runner-up intents and top-two margins conditional on the predicted intent. Rare predicted/runner-up pairs or atypical margins within such pairs indicate unfamiliar classifier competition structure.

Rather than relying only on the nearest angular prototype, this score measures aggregate cosine support from the full set of known intent directions. OOS queries should have weak soft-nearest prototype support.

Predictive entropy captures uncertain intent competition, while distance to the classifier-selected intent centroid captures representation support. Class-conditional training empirical tails put both signals on a shared scale without using evaluation statistics.

content.method: For the Outlier-Exposure confidence objective, use the in-distribution score \(s(x)=\operatorname{logsumexp}(z)-\operatorname{mean}(z)\), where \(z\) are the classifier logits; larger scores indicate more in-distribution-like (equivalently, this is the cross-entropy to a uniform class distribution). In NumPy: `s = np.logaddexp.reduce(logits, axis=-1) - logits.mean(axis=-1)`; cached feature vectors are not needed for this score.

content.method: Fit PCA to centered ID features, let \(V\) contain the retained high-variance principal vectors, and compute each residual norm \(r=\|(I-VV^\top)(f-\mu)\|_2\) (larger means more OOD).  ViM calibrates \(\alpha=\operatorname{mean}_{ID}(\max_j z_j)/\operatorname{mean}_{ID}(r)\) and uses the OOD score \(\alpha r-\operatorname{logsumexp}(z)\), where \(z\) are classifier logits (larger score is more OOD).

content.method: L2-normalize each cached feature vector, estimate normalized per-class means and a shared covariance (and its inverse) on training features, then score a sample by the negative Mahalanobis distance to its nearest class mean: `score = -min_c (z-mu[c]) @ cov_inv @ (z-mu[c])`. After removing the subspace spanned by intent mean differences, in-scope examples should still lie near a shared low-dimensional nuisance manifold in the remaining coordinates. L2-normalized bottleneck and encoder Mahalanobis distances capture complementary near-intent and far-domain novelty. Train-fitted robust tail scaling and covariance-aware positive weights prevent the more variable or redundant view from dominating.

content.method: For each layer (including logits), compute an OOD distance/novelty score \(d_\ell(x)\) against cached ID training features, convert it to an ID-calibrated upper-tail empirical p-value \(p_\ell(x)=(1+\#\{d_\ell^{cal}\ge d_\ell(x)\})/(n_{cal}+1)\), then use Fisher fusion \(S(x)=-2\sum_\ell\log p_\ell(x)\). Declare high \(S\) OOD (or compute \(1-\mathrm{CDF}_{\chi^2(2L)}(S)\)); the per-layer distance can be any distance-based detector such as k-NN distance or Mahalanobis distance.

content.method: Average each example’s Transformer hidden-state vectors across layers to obtain \(z\), then score \(z\) by its empirical projection depth against training vectors \(z_i\): for many random unit directions \(u\), compute \(p_u=\frac1n\sum_i\mathbf1[u^\top z_i\le u^\top z]\) and average \(\min(p_u,1-p_u)\) over \(u\). A generalized winner-versus-rivals logit score captures uncertainty spread across all competing intents, while predicted-intent Mahalanobis surprise measures whether the representation supports that decision. Class-conditional train-fitted tail maps put the complementary cues on a common scale.

The sorted cumulative Dirichlet-evidence profile measures how evidence is distributed across intents independently of total concentration and vacuity. Class-conditional deviation from the train-fitted profile flags atypically diffuse or concentrated evidence shapes.
Low-energy queries retain the classifier energy score, while queries whose energy is already atypical are reranked by train-calibrated pooled-space neighborhood support.
A predicted intent should satisfy its own coordinate-wise variance constraints, but OOS inputs often produce many moderate residual violations rather than only a large total Mahalanobis radius.

After projecting out the class-mean discriminative subspace, in-scope examples should retain locally supported residual variation. Class-scaled Euclidean kNN distance in this residual space flags novel semantic components while preserving residual magnitude information.

A ViM-style residual isolates feature components unsupported by the in-scope principal subspace. Aggregating coordinate-wise residual exceedances beyond train-fitted high quantiles emphasizes broad novel semantic content without relying only on residual L2 magnitude.

A query should be supported by nearby examples from the classifier-selected intent, not merely by nearby examples from any known intent. Multi-radius normalized pooled-feature neighborhoods reduce sensitivity to accidental individual neighbors.

Low-variance within-class directions retain constrained residual structure that OOS inputs often violate. Class-selected empirical projection depth in this trailing subspace flags representations lying in sparse or extreme in-scope regions.

An in-scope query should lie at a typical feature-space radius from the mean of the intent chosen by the classifier. Robust, predicted-intent-specific calibration exposes cases where the logit decision is unsupported by that intent's representation cluster.

In-scope predictions have intent-specific relationships between the decisive top-two margin and the aggregate support of the remaining rivals. Joint surprise in this winner-versus-field shape detects atypical logit competition beyond energy or maximum probability.

Unusual normalized winner dominance captures atypical classifier competition, while pooled-space neighbor distance detects representations unsupported by known examples. Train-fitted empirical tail maps place both signals on a common OOS scale.

EDL in-scope examples should exhibit a learned agreement between normalized Dirichlet evidence allocation and discriminative softmax allocation. Class-conditional surprise in this allocation-agreement shape flags unfamiliar evidential competition without being a monotone function of energy or vacuity.

Training-supported low-energy predictions retain the energy ranking, while items in the uncertain-energy regime are ranked by classifier-selected pooled-feature support. Predicted-class robust calibration avoids penalizing intents with naturally broad clusters.
A classifier winner that is unusually far under its own shrunk diagonal covariance is suspect, especially when the runner-up intent has stronger class-conditional density support.

After removing the class-mean discriminative subspace, each known intent retains a low-dimensional residual variation pattern. Queries whose residual cannot be reconstructed by the classifier-selected intent's residual subspace are likely OOS.

Bottleneck Mahalanobis distance is sensitive to nearby held-out intent shifts, while pooled encoder distance captures broader domain novelty. Train-fitted robust tail scales make their additive fusion comparable without using evaluation statistics.

Rather than ranking only by residual magnitude, this score measures the fraction of a representation's centered energy lying outside the train-fitted principal subspace. It flags angular departures from the in-scope feature manifold while reducing sensitivity to overall feature norm.

Angular pooled representations from in-scope queries should have support at both very local and broader neighborhood scales. Averaging several L2-normalized kNN radii reduces sensitivity to an accidental close neighbor while retaining global semantic-manifold novelty.
Within-class trailing covariance directions are tightly constrained, but OOS inputs can produce an atypical cross-direction residual-shape distribution rather than only a large radius.

Known-intent representations tend to have a class-conditional prototype isolation gap: their nearest intent prototype is meaningfully closer than the runner-up. OOS queries often occupy ambiguous regions between known intent clusters, producing an unusually small relative gap.

In-scope decisions tend to have a characteristic hierarchy between the winner-runner-up gap, the runner-up-third gap, and overall centered logit scale. Class-conditioned surprise in this three-part separation shape flags unfamiliar competition patterns beyond energy or maximum probability.

The Gini coefficient of normalized Dirichlet concentrations measures how unevenly evidence is allocated across intents while discarding total evidence magnitude. Predicted-intent-specific two-sided tail calibration flags unusually diffuse or unusually concentrated evidential allocations.
Energy is preserved exactly for train-calibrated confident predictions, while uncertain predictions are ranked by their classifier-selected pooled-space support after intent-specific calibration.

A classifier-selected intent should be plausible under its own shrunk diagonal variance profile. OOS inputs often have both an unusually large standardized radius and residual energy concentrated in coordinates that are stable for the selected intent.
Class-mean directions capture representation variation that separates known intents; an isolation forest on the orthogonal remainder detects unsupported residual semantics.

Shrunk diagonal class-conditional densities capture complementary near-intent deviations in bottleneck space and broader semantic shifts in pooled encoder space. Train-fitted minimum-variance weights account for correlation between the two in-scope surprise signals.
A ViM-style residual measures encoder content outside the principal in-scope feature subspace, while train-calibrated energy retains classifier uncertainty information for residual-supported inputs.

A locally normalized kNN score compares a query's distance to nearby training examples against the neighborhood radii of those examples. This flags points that are isolated relative to the local in-scope manifold, rather than merely far from a globally dense region.

Low-variance within-class residual directions are tightly constrained for supported intents. A class-conditioned random-hyperplane code measures whether an item's whitened trailing residual has a previously unsupported directional signature.

For each classifier-selected intent, in-scope representations have a characteristic relationship between logit confidence and distance from that intent's feature prototype. A large class-conditional distance residual indicates that the predicted intent is not geometrically supported even after accounting for decision confidence.

In-scope intents have characteristic changes in predictive entropy as the logits are tempered from sharp to soft distributions. Class-conditional surprise in this temperature-response curve detects unusual winner-versus-rival competition beyond energy or maximum probability.
In-scope examples should have both strong angular support from a prototype and a clear cosine margin over competing prototypes. Low train-calibrated support or prototype ambiguity indicates OOS.
Predictive entropy captures unusual classifier competition, while the Mahalanobis distance to the classifier-selected intent captures whether that decision has pooled-feature support.

The sorted normalized Dirichlet concentration spectrum has an elbow structure describing how evidence separates a leading coalition of intents from weaker alternatives. Class-conditioned novelty of this spectrum can flag unfamiliar evidential competition without using total evidence or vacuity.

Energy is used unchanged for train-calibrated confident predictions, but uncertain predictions are routed to a class-selected pooled-feature support score. This prevents uncertain examples from retaining nearly the same energy-only ordering when their representation is poorly supported by the predicted intent.

content.method: Fit principal space \(P\) on cached ID training features and a constant \(\alpha\); for feature \(x\) and classifier logits \(z\), compute residual norm \(r=\|x-\mathrm{proj}_P(x)\|_2\), append virtual logit \(v=\alpha r\), and use \(\mathrm{softmax}([z,v])[-1]=\exp(v)/(\sum_i\exp(z_i)+\exp(v))\) as the OOD score.
content.query: ViM virtual-logit matching residual space out-of-distribution score
content.title: ViM: Out-Of-Distribution with Virtual-logit Matching

content.rationale: A classifier-selected intent should have a better class-specific diagonal Gaussian fit than its strongest logit rival. OOS inputs are penalized when they are both unlikely under the selected intent and geometrically better explained by a competing intent.

After removing the class-mean discriminative subspace, in-scope queries should retain class-supported residual semantic patterns. A class-conditional random Fourier support score detects residual directions that are poorly represented by the predicted intent without relying only on residual magnitude.

Classifier-selected class densities in bottleneck and pooled encoder spaces capture near-intent and far-domain shifts respectively. Per-predicted-intent robust calibration and train-fitted minimum-variance weights make their additive surprise signals comparable.
